messages:
Asha: FYI I surfaced a perf regression on canary after the kernel-selector change. 95th latency up ~18% for mid-length requests (64-256 tokens).
Ben: Ugh. repro trace?
Asha: Pasted flamegraph from last-night's run (sanitized):
```
flamegraph: runtime_select() -> choose_kernel_v2 -> batcher_wait -> kv_lookup_miss -> kernel_launch
hotspots: choose_kernel_v2: 42%  kv_lookup: 28%  cuda_launch: 12%
```
Priya: kv_lookup_miss at that scale suggests namespace mismatch or key salting changed by selector. Did the autotuner start adding seqlen tags to keys?
Asha: Yes — the v2 autotuner began adding seqlen_bucket and arch_tag in the key. That reduced cache reuse across similar requests.
Luca: So we're trading more accurate kernel picks for worse KV hit rate. We should consider timing-buckets for kernel selection rather than explicit per-seqlen keys. Basically bucket latency of the kernel microbench and pick by timing cluster.
Ben: Can you sketch the timing-buckets config?
Luca: Something like:
```
kernel_policy: {
  mode: "timing_buckets",
  buckets_ms: [0.6, 1.2, 2.5, 5.0],
  fallback: "nearest_bucket",
  preserve_kv_namespace: true
}
```
Devon: preserve_kv_namespace true is key — we must avoid changing key shape on driver upgrades. Instead attach a small kernel-hint tag in metadata that doesn't affect keying.
Priya: Agree. Also propose a lightweight decay-based persistence: when driver/model changes, keep old key entries alive for N minutes and gradually migrate on warm hits. That prevents thundering misses on rollout.
Asha: For rollout we saw a thundering migration: earlier runs had 80% hits then new release dropped to 12% and latency spiked. Want an algorithmic approach to smooth it.
Ben: What about a two-phase invalidation: 1) soft compatibility mode where selector treats legacy keys as valid and maps into a bucket; 2) hard rotate after a window.
Luca: Exactly. Implementation sketch: keep (namespace:vX) and (namespace:vX+1) concurrently. Selector tries vX+1, falls back to vX if miss. Background migrator copies hot keys async.
Devon: We'll need to instrument the migrator to avoid IO storms. Use sampling and rate limit (e.g., 50 keys/sec per shard) + bloom filter to detect hotset.
Priya: Also add per-bucket telemetry: kv_hit_rate_by_bucket, kernel_choice_stability, median_latency_by_bucket. We don't have good dashboards for bucket churn today.
perf-bot: ALERT: canary-143 kernel-select-change produced 18% 95th latency regression at 02:14 UTC. Trace id: cf2a8d.
Asha: Perf-bot matched what we saw. Next steps: (1) revert key shape change in autotuner -> ship timing_buckets mode; (2) implement soft-compat fallback and async hotkey migrator; (3) add dashboard panels for kv_hit_rate_by_bucket and migrator throughput.
Ben: I'll pick up the revert + timing_buckets config.
Luca: I'll prototype the migrator + bloom filter & rate limit.
Priya: I'll own the telemetry and dashboard PR.
Devon: I'll add tests simulating driver/model rollouts with synthetic traffic to measure hit-rate decay.
Asha: Thanks. Please ping this thread with PR links and perf numbers. :thumbsup:
